patients.summary: Former construction site supervisor with intermediate-risk AML diagnosed 2023, in remission on maintenance azacitidine/venetoclax at an outside cancer center, with hypertension and chemotherapy-induced neuropathy; joins the practice in 2024. Febrile neutropenia admission in December 2025, ICU stay for severe sepsis in February 2026, and in July 2026 an ICU admission for severe hyponatremia complicated by central pontine myelinolysis with a locked-in state.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT

54M transferring primary care. Main reason: wants one doctor he can reach between oncology visits, since the cancer center is an hour each way.

Oncologic hx (per pt, cancer center records requested): AML, told intermediate-risk cytogenetics, diagnosed March 2023 after a marrow biopsy. Port placed R chest wall at diagnosis. Inpatient induction then consolidation that year, in remission since. Since early 2024 on maintenance cycles: shots at the infusion center for a week each month plus venetoclax pills for two weeks. Several marrow biopsies so far, all OK per him. Prophylactic acyclovir and posaconazole the whole time. Oxycodone from oncology for bone aches, uses it maybe a few times a month.

Neuropathy: numb, pins-and-needles feeling in both feet since the consolidation chemo in 2023. Not painful enough to want a med. Has learned to look at his feet going down stairs. No falls.

HTN since about 2016, amlodipine 5 for years. No home cuff.

PSH: port 2023, marrow biopsies, tonsillectomy as a kid.
Allergies: Bactrim, anaphylaxis. IV contrast, hives.
Meds: reconciled from bottles, see list. Venetoclax 70 mg (7 x 10 mg) days 1-14 is the reduced dose oncology uses with the posaconazole.
FH: father lung ca, died 68. Mother DM2, HTN. Paternal uncle died at 55 of an acute leukemia, type unknown.
SH: construction site supervisor, out on disability since the diagnosis. Lives alone, single. Former smoker, ~20 pk-yr, quit 2019. Beer once or twice a week. No drugs.

ROS: energy okay between cycles, tired the week of injections. No fevers. Bowels slow on oxycodone days, uses Miralax-type powder. Otherwise negative.

EXAM
Vitals as charted. Well appearing, pleasant.
HEENT: oropharynx clear, no mucosal lesions. Neck supple, no nodes.
Chest: port R upper chest, skin intact, no erythema or tenderness.
CV: RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally.
Abd: soft, nontender, no hepatosplenomegaly palpable.
Skin: no petechiae or bruising.
Neuro: alert, fluent. Strength 5/5 throughout. Vibration and pinprick reduced in both feet up to the ankles; proprioception at the toes intact. Gait steady.
Ext: no edema.

A/P
1. AML in remission on maintenance - managed by the cancer center. Records request sent. They run his counts; I'll copy them on my labs.
2. HTN - at goal on amlodipine 5. Continue, I'll take over refills.
3. Chemo neuropathy, feet - stable, declines medication. Foot care and fall precautions talked through.
4. Health maintenance: CMP, lipids, A1c, one-time hep C and HIV today. Colonoscopy 2020 normal per prior records. Tdap 2019. Talked about vaccines for someone on chemo - flu, COVID and Prevnar 20 at a nurse visit next month, Shingrix after that. Qualifies by age and smoking history for a lung screening CT; we agreed to hold off while he's on active leukemia treatment and revisit. PHQ-9 3.
5. Bowel regimen ok.

RTC 3 months, sooner prn. He has my cell for texting.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Randall - your labs from Wednesday look good. Kidney and liver tests normal, sugar and A1c normal, cholesterol fine without a medication. Hep C and HIV screens were negative, so those never need repeating unless something changes. The nurse will reach out to set up your vaccine visit. - your PCP

documents.title: Hematology-oncology treatment summary (received)
documents.author: hematology-oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CANCER CENTER - LEUKEMIA PROGRAM
Treatment summary prepared at the request of the patient's new primary care physician.

Diagnosis: acute myeloid leukemia, intermediate-risk cytogenetics. Diagnosed March 2023 on bone marrow aspirate and biopsy. Right chest wall implanted port placed March 2023.

Treatment:
- Induction with cytarabine-based intensive chemotherapy, spring 2023. Day-28 marrow: morphologic remission.
- Consolidation with cytarabine-based cycles, summer-fall 2023. Peripheral neuropathy of the feet developed during consolidation and has persisted.
- Maintenance since early 2024: azacitidine 75 mg/m2 subcutaneously days 1-7 with venetoclax days 1-14 of each 28-day cycle. Venetoclax 70 mg daily, reduced for concomitant posaconazole.

Most recent marrow (spring 2024): continued morphologic remission.

Supportive medications: acyclovir 800 mg twice daily; posaconazole delayed-release 300 mg daily; oxycodone 5 mg every 6 hours as needed for bone pain; polyethylene glycol as needed.

Allergies: sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (anaphylaxis); iodinated contrast (hives).

Other: hypertension on amlodipine. Former smoker.

Plan: maintenance cycles monthly with counts before each cycle; marrow surveillance periodically. Please call the leukemia nurse line for fever of 100.4 or higher.

Attending hematologist-oncologist, leukemia program

Health risk assessment (pt-completed form reviewed): lives alone, independent with daily activities and errands, drives. Hearing fine, vision fine with readers. No falls in the past year; feet numb, is careful on uneven ground. Diet ok, appetite dips in his injection week. Walks most days. Seatbelt, smoke detectors yes.
PHQ-2: 1. Cognition: conversation and recall normal, no concerns raised.

- Lung: LDCT eligible; still deferring during active leukemia therapy, revisit if treatment ends.

REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT - PHYSICIAN RECORD
Visit 12/10/2025, arrived 13:50.

CC: fevers and shaking chills x 2 days.

HPI: 55-year-old man with AML in remission on monthly maintenance chemotherapy at an outside cancer center; most recent cycle finished about three weeks ago. Two days of fever with chills at home. Sent in by the leukemia nurse line.

PMH: AML (intermediate-risk cytogenetics), hypertension, chemotherapy-related neuropathy of the feet. PSH: R chest port 2023, bone marrow biopsies (latest September), tonsillectomy.
Meds: acyclovir 800 mg BID, posaconazole DR 300 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, polyethylene glycol prn, oxycodone 5 mg q6h prn; maintenance azacitidine/venetoclax per oncology.
Allergies: SULFAMETHOXAZOLE-TRIMETHOPRIM - anaphylaxis. IODINATED CONTRAST - hives.
Social: ex-smoker 20 pk-yr, quit 2019; social alcohol.
Family: father lung cancer, mother DM2/HTN, paternal uncle acute leukemia.

Triage: T 38.9 C (102 F), BP 100/60, HR 110, RR 22.

Exam: pale. Mucosal ulcerations throughout the mouth. Port site without erythema. Lungs clear. Heart tachycardic, regular. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin without rash. No other abnormal findings.

Labs: WBC 1.0 K/uL; ANC 0.1 K/uL (100/uL); Hgb 8.2 g/dL; Plt 50 K/uL. Blood cultures x2 (peripheral and port) drawn - pending at time of admission.

MDM: febrile neutropenia after chemotherapy with mucositis. Cefepime 2 g IV given after cultures. Oncology contacted; admit.

Dx: Chemotherapy-induced neutropenia with fever. Oral mucositis.
Disposition: admitted to the oncology service.

ED attending

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary (received)
documents.author: hematology-oncology
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - ONCOLOGY SERVICE DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 12/10/2025. Discharged 12/15/2025.

Principal diagnosis: febrile neutropenia due to chemotherapy (chemotherapy-induced neutropenia).
Secondary: oral mucositis; AML in remission on maintenance; hypertension; peripheral neuropathy.

Course: Admitted from the ED on IV cefepime, which was continued. Defervesced on hospital day 2. Blood cultures from the port and a peripheral site had no growth at 5 days. Mouth care and topical measures for mucositis; eating soft foods by discharge. Neutrophil count recovered over the stay and cefepime was stopped. Acyclovir and posaconazole continued throughout.

Discharge condition: stable, afebrile, ambulating.
Discharge medications: unchanged from home - acyclovir 800 mg BID, posaconazole DR 300 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, polyethylene glycol prn, oxycodone 5 mg q6h prn. Next maintenance cycle on hold until he sees his oncologist.

Allergies: sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (anaphylaxis), iodinated contrast (hives).

Follow-up: leukemia program in 1 week; primary care within 1 week.

Hospitalist, oncology service

Now: no fevers at home, checking temp twice a day. Mouth much better, a couple of sore spots left. Appetite returning. Tired but up and about. Taking amlodipine.

Exam: vitals as charted, afebrile. Looks tired but well. A few healing shallow ulcers on the buccal mucosa, no thrush. Port clean. Lungs clear, heart regular. No edema.

A/P:
- Chemotherapy-induced neutropenia, febrile episode, recovered: problem list updated. Oncology sees him Monday and will decide on the next cycle and dosing.
- Mucositis healing: salt-water rinses, soft diet a few more days.
- HTN: amlodipine 5, fine.
Meds reconciled, no changes. Fever precautions reviewed again. F/u per routine, text with any fever.

documents.title: Question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Back on the shots since the end of Dec. Is there anything I should be doing different so I don't end up in the hospital again? Feel ok right now.

documents.title: RE: Question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good question. Keep doing what you did right: take your temperature any time you feel off, and call the leukemia line right away for 100.4 or higher, day or night. Keep taking the acyclovir and posaconazole every day. Hand washing, avoid sick contacts when your counts are down, and keep up with mouth care. You're up to date on your vaccines. Text me anytime.

documents.title: ICU and Hospital Discharge Summary (received)
documents.author: critical care medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 02/25/2026 via the ED to the medical ICU. Transferred to the floor 03/02/2026. Discharged home 03/05/2026.

Principal diagnosis: severe sepsis with hemodynamic instability, source not identified.
Secondary: hyponatremia, transient; AML on maintenance therapy; hypertension; chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy; history of chemotherapy-induced neutropenia in December 2025.

Hospital course:
The patient, 55, with AML in remission on azacitidine/venetoclax maintenance, was admitted in the early morning of 02/25 with sepsis and unstable pressures. He received IV fluid resuscitation and broad-spectrum IV antibiotics and required norepinephrine, which was weaned off over the first days in the unit. No source was identified.

Electrolytes were followed with a morning chemistry each day. Serum sodium, in mEq/L, by ICU day: day 1 (2/25) 136; day 2 (2/26) 142; day 3 (2/27) 131; day 4 (2/28) 139. Daily IV fluid volumes varied over this period; the values were not felt to reflect acute dilution, and there was no hemolysis or laboratory error. Nephrology was consulted for the swings and advised continued daily chemistries and careful fluid choices; sodium remained normal after day 4.

Antibiotics were completed in hospital. Port remained in place. Home prophylaxis continued.

Discharge medications: acyclovir 800 mg BID; posaconazole DR 300 mg daily; amlodipine 5 mg daily; polyethylene glycol 17 g daily prn; oxycodone 5 mg q6h prn. Maintenance chemotherapy on hold pending oncology review.

Allergies: sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (anaphylaxis); iodinated contrast (hives).

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week with a BMP; leukemia program in 2 weeks.

ICU attending / hospitalist

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Discharge summary received this morning. Reached pt: home since Thursday, weak and sleeping a lot but no fever, eating and drinking ok, no dizziness standing. Taking all meds including amlodipine. Hospital wants a BMP this week. Booked Wed 3/11 10:00 with PCP; will draw at the visit.

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM, high complexity. ICU 2/25-3/2, home 3/5: severe sepsis, no source found, needed pressors briefly. Sodium bounced around in the unit (136, 142, 131, 139 on the first four mornings) and nephrology followed; normal after that.

Today: worn out, sleeping 10 hours, slowly walking more each day. No fever, chills, cough, urinary symptoms or diarrhea. Mouth fine. Drinking normally, no special fluid habits. Has not had a maintenance cycle since February; oncology visit 3/19.

Exam: vitals as charted, afebrile, BP fine on amlodipine. Tired but alert, oriented, conversant. Mucous membranes moist. Port site clean, no tenderness. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abd soft. No edema. Neuro: nonfocal apart from his known stocking sensory loss.

A/P:
- Severe sepsis: treated, resolved clinically. Off problem list as active.
- Hyponatremia during the ICU stay: single low value, resolved there; BMP today to confirm.
- AML: oncology to decide on restarting maintenance.
- HTN: continue amlodipine 5.
Meds reconciled against the discharge list, no changes. Will message BMP result.

events.reason: altered mental status and severe hyponatremia

reports.text:
Indication: acute unresponsiveness after correction of severe hyponatremia; quadriplegia.
Technique: multiplanar multisequence MRI of the brain without intravenous contrast.
Findings: symmetric T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the central pons with sparing of the tegmentum. No other signal abnormality in the brainstem, cerebellum or cerebral hemispheres. No acute hemorrhage. No mass effect or midline shift. Ventricles and sulci normal in size for age. Major intracranial flow voids present.
reports.conclusion: Symmetric central pontine T2/FLAIR hyperintensity sparing the tegmentum, consistent with central pontine myelinolysis.

documents.title: Neurology ICU Consultation (received)
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - NEUROLOGY CONSULTATION, NEUROSCIENCES ICU
Date of consultation: 07/28/2026. Copy sent to primary care through case management.

Reason for consult: acute unresponsiveness.

HPI: 56-year-old man with AML on maintenance therapy, hospitalized in December 2025 for febrile neutropenia and in February 2026 in the ICU for severe sepsis. Brought in 07/25 with altered mental status; admission serum sodium 112 mEq/L. Treated in the ICU with IV hypertonic saline. Sodium rose to 137 mEq/L over the next 48 hours. On hospital day 3 (07/27) he became acutely unresponsive; he was intubated for inability to breathe on his own and is on mechanical ventilation.

Allergies: sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (anaphylaxis); iodinated contrast (hives).
Home meds: acyclovir, posaconazole DR, amlodipine, polyethylene glycol prn, oxycodone prn; maintenance azacitidine/venetoclax.

Exam (off sedation): eyes open; blinks reliably to command and follows commands with blinks. Complete quadriplegia. No facial movement. No speech. No spontaneous respirations over the ventilator.

Imaging: MRI brain 07/28 - symmetric hyperintensity of the central pons sparing the tegmentum.

Impression: central pontine myelinolysis (osmotic demyelination) presenting with a locked-in state, in the setting of severe hyponatremia and its correction.

Recommendations: supportive ICU care and ventilation; communication by blink code with nursing; neurology will follow.

Neurology attending

documents.title: Call from hospital case manager
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Case manager from the regional hospital ICU called: pt admitted Saturday 7/25 with confusion and a very low sodium, now in the ICU on a ventilator after a neurologic decline on 7/27. They requested our current med list and allergy list and the name of his oncology team. Faxed med list, allergies (TMP-SMX anaphylaxis, contrast hives) and the leukemia program's contact. Asked that the neurology and discharge records be sent to us. PCP informed.
